lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Everything important was there—almost. The project printed clean, the folder labeled, the forms signed. But the certificate wasn’t stamped until a day too late, or the final upload missed the minute hand by a sliver.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the counter, the secretary didn’t argue. She didn’t gloat. She just pointed at the time and said the one thing that couldn’t be negotiated: "Deadline was final."

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: People later said you had potential. They talked about your project in class. They used your work as an example of what could have been. Your name, however, never appeared on the list.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You learn the quiet lesson the hard way: excellence without timing is still a miss. Next time, you’ll be early, not perfect. And that will be enough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Potential isn’t a promise. It’s a plan, waiting for you to move on it before the clock runs out.
